time_scope: contemporary system analyzed from the 26,000-entry Kalmyk-Russian Dictionary (1977)
claim: Suseeva's modern analysis gives a sharp positional split: /o/ and /ö/ occur only in the first syllable, whether stressed or unstressed; the central/back-front reduced vowels transcribed <ъ> and <e> occur in noninitial syllables and, when stressed, only word-finally.
formal_environment: Vowel phoneme distribution by syllable position
normalized_environment: O,Ö -> SYLLABLE1_ONLY; REDUCED_ъ,e -> NONINITIAL_ONLY and STRESSED only FINAL
scope: Suseeva 2025 phonological analysis of modern Kalmyk dictionary forms
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Suseeva notes a derivational exception to ordinary /o/ positional behavior: the negative element historically from uga has become suffix -go with final [o], including after both back- and front-vowel bases; this should not be erased by the first-syllable generalization.

time_scope: contemporary system analyzed from the 26,000-entry Kalmyk-Russian Dictionary (1977)
claim: The derivational suffix -go, historically from the negative particle uga 'not/no', places [o] outside the otherwise first-syllable-only distribution of /o/. It occurs after both front- and back-harmonic bases, making it an explicit morphology-conditioned exception to a simple word-level positional/harmonic restriction.
normalized_environment: MORPHEME[-go] licenses NONINITIAL_O across FRONT/BACK bases
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This exception is specifically morphological and diachronic; it does not show general productive licensing of noninitial /o/ in lexical roots.

time_scope: contemporary system analyzed from the 26,000-entry Kalmyk-Russian Dictionary (1977)
claim: Suseeva argues that vowel length is not phonemic in modern Kalmyk but is acquired by ordinary vowels under stress: six vowel phonemes can occur stressed or unstressed across syllables, with stressed realizations long and unstressed realizations short. The article treats pairs traditionally cited for phonemic length as stress-placement contrasts instead.

source_forms.analysis: no long-vowel phonemes; stressed vowels acquire length

normalized_environment: STRESS adds VOWEL_DURATION; LENGTH analyzed as nonphonemic
scope: Suseeva 2025 analysis; not automatically reconciled with traditional Kalmyk descriptions
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This is an explicit reanalysis that conflicts with sources treating long vowels as phonemic; preserve as analytical disagreement rather than replacing the inventory denominator.

time_scope: contemporary system analyzed from the 26,000-entry Kalmyk-Russian Dictionary (1977)
claim: Suseeva treats first-syllable vowels as positionally strong even when unstressed because synharmonism makes them determine the front/back class of following vowels (and sometimes consonants); consequently first-syllable vowels are described as acoustically/articulatorily clear under both stressed and unstressed conditions.

source_forms.conditioning: determines row/front-back quality of following vowels, sometimes consonants

normalized_environment: SYLLABLE1 vowel = HARMONY_CLASS controller even when UNSTRESSED
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This record captures Suseeva's synchronic interpretation and should coexist with older Oirat/Kalmyk descriptions rather than silently resolve differences in harmony formalization.
